Ibn Arabi said, "العبد رب و الرب عبد" or "al-`abd-u rabb-un wa-r-rabb-u `abd-un" (the slave is the lord and the lord is the slave)." Sufis claim that such statements were always considered to be the most elevated exposition of mystical thought in Islam, and therefore unsuitable for the untrained mind. Ibn Arabi has also said, "الرب رب في التنزل والعبد عبد في الترقى" or "ar-rabb-u rabb-un f? t-tanazzul-i wa-l-`abd-u `abd-un f? t-taraqq?" (The lord is a lord in his descent [to his creations] and a slave is a slave in rising). in Fusoos Al-Hikam" and "Al-Ahkaam. answer: Miscellaneous >> Tasawwuf Question ID: 31812 Country: Pakistan Title: I want to do a wazefa or wird with one of The Allah names so what is difference nd which is right and why. e.g. Al-rehman or Ya-rehman Question: I want to do a wazefa or wird with one of The Allah names so what is difference nd which is right and why. e.g. Al-rehman or Ya-rehman? Answer ID: 31812 Posted on: Sep 1, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 696/585/B=1432) If you have liking towards recitation of wazifah you should recite the following wazifah which is the best, most useful and on which is agreed upon by all pious elders. That is as follows: Istighfar (أستغفرالله الذى لا اله إلا هو الحى القيوم و أتوب إليه) 100 times and لا إله الا الله محمد رسول الله 100 times, durood 100 times, سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا اله إلا الله والله اكبر ولا حول وقلا قوة إلا بالله العلى العظيم 100 times every day in the morning and evening. It is not proved to recite the wazifah of Ya Rahman and Ya Al-Rahman from hadith. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
